title: hs_junk_lookup
claim_boundary: Typical contents of discarded devices; a donor's parts are unknown until it is opened and tested.

title: keep the vacuum body
choice: Keep the vacuum's own chassis, wheels, laser scanner, pack, bumper and cliff sensors in place; replace only what is dead
because: The body already holds every module at the right height and the scanned STEP models are too coarse to place mounting holes on a new chassis
alternatives: strip the modules onto a printed chassis (needs the modules' mounting holes measured)
OOMWOO One (in development, ~US$200 of new spares)

title: route by what the donor's main board does
choice: Route A: board works -> Valetudo (local control and map) plus the phone as camera. Route B: board dead -> ESP32-S3 with two DRV8871 for the wheels and a MOSFET for the scanner motor
because: Route A needs no new electronics; route B uses the measured wheel module pinout and kaiaai/LDS, which needs an external motor driver for the LDS02RR
alternatives: Raspberry Pi with ROS2 on board (more power, more cost)

title: hs_size_rover_drive
summary: 25 of 40 gearmotor options pass; best pololu-25d-mp-12v 99:1
claim_boundary: Linear DC-motor model between the maker's no-load and (extrapolated) stall points at nominal voltage; Pololu says units stall well before the listed point as they heat. No battery sag, wheel slip or turning losses.

title: hs_energy_budget
claim_boundary: Sizing calculation from stated loads and ratings. Nothing was built or measured. Runtime and surge must be tested with the real loads, and AC wiring, residual current protection and earthing need a qualified electrician.

loads.name: LDS02RR laser scanner, motor and electronics (declared 2.0 W, not measured)
ESP32-S3 over Wi-Fi (declared 0.6 W) through a 5 V buck at 90%
phone streaming its camera, charged from the pack (declared 3.0 W) through the buck at 90%
2 wheel modules cruising (0.204 A each at 14.4 V, hs_size_rover_drive)
